summary: Your report is well structured and balanced, with a clear recommendation and relevant cases (HSSIB, Volkswagen). You identify ethical issues and stakeholders well. However, evidence is thin, some arguments are speculative, EACE clause 2.3b is misapplied, references are incomplete, and no visual elements are used. Most scenario requirements are met; R2, R3 and R6 only partially.
next_steps: Add quantitative evidence (e.g., defect rates, recall costs, injury statistics) and correct all references: provide a URL for [3], fix the malformed URL in [1], and correct the author formatting in [4].

Deepen stakeholder analysis: give decision-making recommendations for the chip contractor, health department, and end-users, and replace speculative claims (e.g., competitor-will-ship) with supported reasoning.
Include at least one visual element (stakeholder map or decision flowchart) and proofread for language slips (e.g., 'DICUSSION') to raise C5.

criteria.C1: You clearly identify ethical issues, link them to engineering design and organisational competition, and list stakeholders in the Introduction. This meets Excellent. To sustain this level, carry the stakeholder analysis through the body so each group’s interests are revisited in the discussion.
criteria.C2: You present balanced for-and-against arguments and a clear conclusion, but depth is moderate and recommendations focus mainly on Rachel and her company. To reach Excellent, deepen the arguments and make decision-making recommendations for several distinct stakeholders (e.g., chip contractor, health department, end-users). Avoid unsupported claims like the competitor-will-ship argument.
criteria.C3: Your report has a logical structure and the conclusion follows from the arguments, but it does not systematically analyse every stakeholder, especially the chip contractor. To reach Excellent, ensure each section builds a compelling case and systematically addresses the ethical issues for all stakeholders, not just Rachel and her company.
criteria.C4: You use relevant external cases (HSSIB, Volkswagen) and the Engineers Australia code, but quantitative evidence is absent and references are limited. To reach Excellent, add quantitative data (e.g., defect rates, recall costs) and strengthen references (complete URLs, correct formatting). Ensure evidence directly supports ethical arguments—the Apple/CNBC example supports consumer release strategy, not shipping defective servers.
criteria.C5: Required sections are present and writing is mostly readable, but there are language slips (e.g., 'DICUSSION'), no figures or tables, and references are incomplete or malformed ([3] lacks URL, [1] malformed URL, [4] incorrect author formatting). To reach Good, proofread for language errors, add at least one visual element (e.g., stakeholder map or decision flowchart), and correct reference formatting.
